claim: For EXIF orientations 5–8 the draft target passed to `img.draft()` is expressed in oriented (swapped) coordinates although `draft()` decodes in the stored orientation, so the decode geometry after `exif_transpose` is wrong and the sampled pixels/Auto statistics can differ for rotated inputs.
reason: Same claimed defect (swapped draft target for orientations 5–8) in the same decode path of one file; the attempts cite different lines of that path.
note: Merge across different cited line ranges (117–123 vs 144–154) within one function; the wording is consistent across the four attempts.

claim: When the Files API accepts the upload but the response has no `urls.get`, the code exits (`process.exit(1)`) before returning the uploaded file id, so `main`'s `finally` cleanup cannot delete the file and it stays in the Replicate account.
reason: Same claimed defect at the same branch of one function in one file; eight attempts, consistent wording.
note: Merge across a 36-line spread of cited lines (178–214); all describe the same branch.

claim: Output images are named with only the first eight characters of `prediction_id`; two runs of one photo sharing that prefix make the later save overwrite the earlier image while both figures reference the same path, so the sheet can show the wrong run.
reason: Same claimed defect at the same site of one file; five attempts, consistent wording.

claim: The new offline decoder (EXIF orientation, ICC conversion, JPEG draft decoding, custom resampling / browser parity) has no tests.
reason: Same claim (this file's decoder is untested) at the same location (the file); kept apart from the harness-wide claim D5 because the location differs.
note: Could be merged into D5 (same 'no tests' claim at directory scope) — kept separate on location.

claim: The PR adds decoding/orientation, ROI, browser-parity, contact-sheet and upload/polling/cleanup behaviour without any tests.
reason: Same claim at the same (directory-level) location; three attempts.

claim: The calibration harness has no tests for its decoding, computed recommendations or record validation.
reason: A 'no tests' claim located at a different file than D4 and D5's directory; separate by the 'another file' rule.
note: Could be merged into D5 (its text is the harness-wide claim); separate on location.

claim: There is no test coverage for an empty scan or for a requested photo with no runs (the testing counterpart of D13).
reason: A testing claim scoped to one file and two cases; separate from D5 (scope) and from D13 (a different claim: missing tests vs the behaviour itself).
note: Could be merged into D5; kept separate on location and specificity.

claim: The comparison tool has no tests for its exit decisions or malformed-input handling.
reason: A 'no tests' claim at a different file; separate by the 'another file' rule.
note: Could be merged into D5; separate on location.

claim: The comparison checks that each new record exists but assumes the baseline record exists and that both carry numeric fields; a missing or malformed baseline entry raises an uncaught exception instead of the documented controlled failure.
reason: One attempt; kept separate from D10, which cites another location and adds a JSON-parse claim.
note: D9 and D10 overlap on 'missing baseline entry'; could be one row 'malformed or missing baseline input is not handled as the documented controlled failure'.

claim: Malformed JSON and unexpected record shapes are not handled as the documented comparison error (exit 1): `JSON.parse` exceptions escape, and missing baseline entries or fields cause unrelated runtime errors during the Auto calculation.
reason: One attempt; a different cited location than D9 and an additional claim (JSON parse errors).

claim: A floored manifest ROI can collapse to zero width or height on small images; `exposure_stats` then averages an empty array and reports NaN.
reason: Single claim at one location.

claim: The exposure diagnostic says it reports encoded RGB values, but converting to RGB does not apply an embedded ICC profile, so for profiled images the values are profile-encoded, not the sRGB the browser/app decode path produces.
reason: Single claim at one location.

claim: For an explicitly requested tuning photo with no runs, `outputs`/`sizes` are empty and `min(sizes, …)` raises `ValueError`; with no requested ids, an empty scan writes an empty index without saying that no runs were found.
reason: Single behavioural claim at one location (D7 is its testing counterpart, a different claim).

claim: The target size is chosen only from the model outputs, so when every output is smaller than the original the original is enlarged against the documented no-enlargement rule; resizing all images to one width×height can also distort differing aspect ratios.
reason: Single claim at one location; a different claim than D3 at a neighbouring line.

claim: The `jpeg-draft` path assumes Pillow's reduced decode still covers the requested sample size; `draft()` can return dimensions smaller than the target and `point_bilinear()` then enlarges, giving different sample pixels than the documented decode-and-downscale method.
reason: A different claim than D1 (undersized draft result, not a swapped target) at a different line of the same file.

claim: When `--all` and positional ids are both supplied, `--all` silently takes precedence and every manifest entry is decoded, including validation inputs.
reason: Single claim at one location.

claim: The sampler clamps source coordinates before deriving interpolation weights; at destination edges this differs from sampling at the pixel-centre coordinate, so the RGBA buffers can disagree with the browser sampler the harness claims to mirror.
reason: Single claim at one location.

claim: With explicitly supplied ids the script assumes each `.meta.json` exists; a typo or a missing decode raises an uncaught filesystem exception instead of a clear harness error.
reason: Single claim at one location.

claim: The parity decision compares summary statistics but never checks the browser sample's natural dimensions against the offline sample dimensions, so a geometry mismatch can be reported as a match.
reason: Single claim at one location.

claim: After a non-OK create response, setting `process.exitCode` and returning only leaves the `if` block; execution continues to parse the error body as a prediction and polls with a missing id instead of terminating.
reason: A different claim than D2 (create failure vs missing upload URL) at a different function of the same file.
